learning_objective: 🎯 Explore modern farming technology! Learn how sensors, GPS, and data analysis make agriculture super smart, efficient, and profitable.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is 'smart farming'. Instead of treating an entire field the exact same way, farmers use technology to give each specific plant exactly what it needs—no more, no less.
Global Positioning System (GPS) helps tractors drive themselves automatically! It also helps map the exact boundaries of the field so farmers don't overlap seeds or fertilizers.
Sensors placed in the soil tell the farmer's smartphone exactly how wet or dry the soil is. The irrigation system turns on automatically only when the plant actually needs water.
Drones fly over fields and take thermal pictures. They can spot which parts of the crop are sick or lacking nutrients, and can even spray pesticides accurately from the air.
It saves massive amounts of water, reduces chemical use, protects the environment, saves money, and increases the total crop yield (output).

fun_activity.title: 📡 Be a Human Sensor!
fun_activity.instructions: Don't just pour water on your house plants every day! Stick your finger one inch into the soil. If it feels wet, don't water it. If it feels dry, water it. You just practiced precision irrigation!

exam_tips: 📌 Define Precision Farming clearly: applying the right treatment in the right place at the right time.
📌 Be able to list 3 technologies used in precision farming (Drones, GPS, Soil Sensors).
📌 Explain how precision farming is better for the environment (prevents over-spraying of chemicals).
quick_recap: ⭐ Precision farming moves agriculture from 'guesswork' to 'data-driven' science.
⭐ Drones save farmers time by surveying hundreds of acres in minutes.
⭐ Technology reduces waste, making farming more sustainable for the future.
